authority: diagnostic: paper only, not investment advice
flags: The company signed a merger agreement and completed its acquisition of Savage on the same day. Savage was merged into the company through a two-step merger, and the seller's designee was appointed to the board.

business_model.claim: Smith & Wesson designs and manufactures firearms and related products, selling them under the Smith & Wesson and Gemtech brands.
quotes: We are one of the world’s leading manufacturers and designers of firearms.

business_model.claim: Its customers are distributors, law enforcement and government or military agencies, and retailers. The product range runs from consumer carry pistols to professional and military rifles.
quotes: Our customers include distributors; federal, state, and municipal law enforcement agencies and officers; government and military agencies; and retailers.

business_model.basis: stated in the P3 sales table
business_model.claim: In the latest full fiscal year net sales were $523,845 (table in thousands). Handguns were the largest category at $394,404, followed by long guns at 90,481 and other products & services at 38,960.

business_model.basis: stated in the P4 sales table
business_model.claim: In the latest quarter net sales were $112,587 (table in thousands), up 32.3% from the prior-year quarter. Handguns were $83,774, long guns 20,381 and other products & services 8,432.

business_model.basis: stated in the P4 units table; the dominance of sporting goods is inferred from those unit counts
business_model.claim: Shipments go mainly through the sporting goods (consumer) channel, with a smaller professional channel. Latest-quarter handgun units were 175 sporting goods and 16 professional, and long gun units were 28 and 5 (units in thousands).

Handgun sales rose $18.8 million, or 29.0%, in the latest quarter. Management attributes this to consumer demand, a shift to higher-priced models, new products, and a 2% to 3% price increase on select products. New products were 43.1% of handgun sales.
quotes: Shipments of new products represented 43.1% of handgun sales in the quarter.

business_model.claim: Product introductions are a core revenue driver. New products were 35.3% of overall net sales in the latest quarter, including one new pistol, one new long gun and many line extensions.
quotes: Newly introduced products represented 35.3% of overall net sales for the three months ended July 31, 2026 and included one new pistol, one new long gun, and many new product line extensions.

business_model.basis: stated in the P2 risk factors
business_model.claim: Revenue is cyclical and sensitive to political and social events and consumer demand. Management says results vary from period to period and that inventory can build above customer demand.
quotes: These concerns often result in an increase in near-term consumer demand for our products and subsequent softening of demand when these concerns subside.
our operating results can vary significantly from period to period

business_model.basis: figures stated in P4; the sell-in versus sell-through interpretation is inferred
business_model.claim: Company shipments into the sporting goods channel can differ from end-consumer demand. In the latest quarter handgun shipments into that channel rose 16.7% while NICS-based handgun demand rose 4.7%.
Cost of sales was 80,317 against net sales of $112,587 (table in thousands) in the latest quarter, giving gross profit of $32,270 and a gross margin of 28.7%.
The latest quarter's gross margin was lifted by $2.9 million of tariff refunds, worth about 260 basis points and described as non-recurring. Excluding them, gross margin was 26.1%.
quotes: Excluding the impact of tariff refunds, gross margin for the three months ended July 31, 2026 was 26.1%.

business_model.claim: Tariffs on imported materials and components are a cost driver. Management estimated they cut gross margin by about 100 basis points in the latest fiscal year, when gross margin was 26.9%.
quotes: We estimate that higher tariffs negatively impacted gross margin by approximately 100 basis points when compared to the comparable period last year.

business_model.basis: stated in P4 and P2; the operating-leverage reading is inferred
business_model.claim: Higher production volume helps margin through fixed-cost absorption. Labor cost is an offset, and the company runs a small number of plants that it must keep efficiently loaded.
quotes: Gross margin was also favorably impacted by fixed-cost absorption from higher production volumes, partially offset by higher labor costs.
We operate in only four facilities located in three locations, and our success depends on our ability to operate each facility efficiently.

business_model.claim: Input costs are exposed to inflation because supplies are bought on short-term commitments, and the company must raise prices to offset it.
quotes: Because we typically purchase these supplies based on short-term commitments from our suppliers, we are exposed to risks associated with significant levels of cost inflation.

business_model.claim: Operating expenses were 28,053 (table in thousands), or 24.9% of sales, in the latest quarter. They were made up of research and development at 2,557, selling, marketing and distribution at 10,158, and general and administrative at 15,338.
quotes: General and administrative expenses increased $2.0 million over the prior year comparable quarter, primarily as a result of higher legal costs and profit-related compensation expenses.

business_model.claim: Other revenue comes from parts, handcuffs, suppressors and contract manufacturing for third parties. It grew $1.9 million, or 29.0%, in the latest quarter on higher parts and suppressor sales.
quotes: Manufacturing Services: We utilize our substantial manufacturing capabilities to provide services to third-party customers.
Other products and services revenue increased $1.9 million, or 29.0%, over the comparable quarter last year, primarily because of higher parts and suppressor sales.

business_model.basis: stated in P4 and F3; the funding link is inferred from the cash flow statement
business_model.claim: The business is working-capital heavy. In the latest quarter inventory rose $24.4 million on level loading, operating cash flow was (8,846), capital spending was (11,929), and loan proceeds were 20,000 (cash flow table in thousands).
quotes: Inventory balances increased $24.4 million between April 30, 2026 and July 31, 2026 as a result of level loading of our manufacturing facilities to ensure our ability to satisfy anticipated future demand.

business_model.claim: Funding comes from a revolving credit line of $175.0 million, of which $40.0 million was outstanding at the latest quarter-end at a weighted average rate of 5.42%.
quotes: As of July 31, 2026, we had $40.0 million of borrowings outstanding on the Revolving Line, bearing interest at a weighted average rate of 5.42%, which is equal to the Adjusted Term SOFR rate plus an applicable margin.

business_model.claim: After the latest quarter the company completed an acquisition of Savage. This adds a business whose revenue and cost contribution are not shown in the evidence.
quotes: On the Closing Date, the Company completed its acquisition of Savage pursuant to the Merger Agreement.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in P1 (Item 1 Business); the share claim is the company's own estimate.
competitive_position.claim: The company describes itself as a leading firearm maker, and it says it holds the leading share of the modern sporting rifle market. Both statements are management's own and unaudited.
quotes: leading manufacturers and designers of firearms
what we estimate is the leading share of the modern sporting rifle market

competitive_position.basis: Stated in P3 (MD&A table and text).
competitive_position.claim: Handguns are the core franchise and grew strongly in fiscal 2026. Handgun net sales rose 18.8% to $394,404 (table in thousands), and new products were 43.6% of handgun sales. A 2% to 3% price increase on select products also contributed.
quotes: Shipments of new products represented 43.6% of handgun sales in the period.

competitive_position.claim: Long guns were a weak spot in fiscal 2026, with net sales down 13.0% to $90,481 (table in thousands) and consumer demand for long guns down 4.6%. They rebounded sharply in the first quarter of fiscal 2027.
quotes: Sales of our long guns decreased $13.5 million, or 13.0%, from fiscal 2025

competitive_position.basis: Shipment and NICS figures are stated in P4; the interpretation that shipments outpaced demand is inferred from comparing them.
competitive_position.claim: In the first quarter of fiscal 2027, sporting-goods handgun shipments grew faster than measured consumer demand. Shipments rose 16.7% against 4.7% growth in NICS-indicated demand. Inventory also rose to 180,661 from 156,250 (table in thousands), which the company says may matter if channel stock exceeds demand.
quotes: overall demand for handguns increased by 4.7%
While inventory levels, both internally and in the distribution channel, in excess of demand may negatively impact future operating results

competitive_position.claim: First-quarter fiscal 2027 gross margin of 28.7% was lifted by a non-recurring $2.9 million of tariff refunds. Excluding the refunds, gross margin was 26.1%, against 25.9% a year earlier.
quotes: Excluding the impact of tariff refunds, gross margin for the three months ended July 31, 2026 was 26.1%.

competitive_position.claim: Tariffs are a named cost threat to margins. The company estimates higher tariffs reduced fiscal 2026 gross margin by about 100 basis points. Its risk factors also flag uncertainty over tariff refunds.
quotes: We estimate that higher tariffs negatively impacted gross margin by approximately 100 basis points when compared to the comparable period last year.

competitive_position.claim: Demand depends on the political and regulatory environment. The company says its demand was hurt in recent years by a perceived lower risk of federal gun control. It also names state restrictions, the possible repeal or reinterpretation of the PLCAA, and a state 'industry accountability' lawsuit in which it is a defendant.
quotes: we believe demand for our products was negatively impacted in recent years by unified Republican control of the executive and legislative branches of the federal government as a result of a perceived lower risk of federal gun control legislation and regulation.
These statutes are being actively enforced, and we are a defendant in one such action.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in P2 as the company's belief.
competitive_position.claim: Inflation is named as a demand and cost threat. The company says some consumers have traded down to lower-priced firearms or delayed purchases, and that input and labor costs have risen.
quotes: certain firearm consumers have traded down to purchase lower-priced firearms or delayed purchases due to cost concerns

competitive_position.basis: Borrowings and capital expenditure guidance are stated in P4. Cash comes from F1 and free cash flow from P6. That the spending is funded partly by debt is inferred from the borrowings.
competitive_position.claim: The company is investing in capacity but financing part of it with debt, which limits financial flexibility. In the first quarter of fiscal 2027 it had $40.0 million drawn on a $175.0 million revolver and cash of 18,699 (table in thousands). First-quarter free cash flow was $(20,775) (table in thousands), and full-year capital expenditure guidance was set at $45.0 million to $50.0 million.
quotes: We currently expect to spend $45.0 million to $50.0 million on capital expenditures in fiscal 2027.
As of July 31, 2026, we had $40.0 million of borrowings outstanding on the Revolving Line

competitive_position.claim: Operations are concentrated and still being relocated. The company runs a small number of facilities, with key components made at an aging Springfield plant, and it must meet Tennessee incentive commitments by 2027 to 2029 or may have to repay part of the award.
quotes: We operate in only four facilities located in three locations, and our success depends on our ability to operate each facility efficiently.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in P7; the effect on competitive position is inferred.
competitive_position.claim: The company completed its acquisition of Savage after the quarter ended, which broadens its footprint in the firearm industry.
quotes: On the Closing Date, the Company completed its acquisition of Savage pursuant to the Merger Agreement.

financial_health.basis: Stated in the balance sheet [F1]; the inventory point is inferred from the line items.
financial_health.claim: Liquidity is adequate on the balance sheet, but cash fell in the quarter. Cash and cash equivalents were 18,699 at July 31, 2026, down from 28,190 at April 30, 2026 (table in thousands). Total current assets of 247,493 compare with total current liabilities of 68,431, and inventories make up most of current assets.

financial_health.basis: Stated in the balance sheet [F1]; the link to the revolver draw is inferred from the cash flow statement [F3].
financial_health.claim: Leverage rose during the quarter. Notes and loans payable were 39,185 at July 31, 2026 versus 19,121 at April 30, 2026. A finance lease payable of 31,676 (net of current portion) is also carried. Total liabilities were 149,602 against stockholders' equity of 373,702 (table in thousands).

financial_health.basis: Stated in the 10-Q MD&A [P4] and the 10-K MD&A [P3] (the $20.0 million figure at April 30, 2026); covenant thresholds are not given.
financial_health.claim: The revolving credit line was drawn to $40.0 million at July 31, 2026, up from $20.0 million at April 30, 2026. The weighted average rate was 5.42%, and the company reports compliance with all debt covenants.
quotes: As of July 31, 2026, we had $40.0 million of borrowings outstanding on the Revolving Line, bearing interest at a weighted average rate of 5.42%, which is equal to the Adjusted Term SOFR rate plus an applicable margin.
We were in compliance with all debt covenants as of July 31, 2026.

financial_health.basis: Stated in the cash flow statement [F3] and the earnings release reconciliation [P6]; the mechanism is drawn from the line items.
financial_health.claim: Cash generation was weak in the first quarter of fiscal 2027. Operating cash flow was (8,846) against net income of 2,588, and capital spending of 11,929 pushed free cash flow to (20,775) (table in thousands). The prior-year quarter showed (8,110) of operating cash flow and (12,401) of free cash flow.

financial_health.basis: Stated in the 10-Q MD&A [P4] and the earnings release [P6].
financial_health.claim: Quarterly earnings quality has two issues: a non-recurring tariff refund helped margin, and profit did not turn into cash. Gross margin was 28.7%, including $2.9 million of tariff refunds that lifted it by about 260 basis points. Excluding them, gross margin was 26.1%.
quotes: These refunds favorably impacted gross margin by approximately 260 basis points and represented a non-recurring benefit.

financial_health.basis: Stated in the 10-K MD&A [P3]; the steady-state comparison is inferred.
financial_health.claim: Full-year fiscal 2026 cash generation was strong but came mainly from working capital release. Operating cash flow was $114.2 million versus $7.2 million of cash used in fiscal 2025, with a $33.6 million decrease in inventory the largest favorable item. That cash funded $60.0 million of net revolver repayment and $23.2 million of dividends.
quotes: Cash provided by operating activities was $114.2 million in fiscal 2026 compared with $7.2 million of cash used in fiscal 2025.

financial_health.basis: Stated in the 10-Q MD&A [P4], 10-K MD&A [P3] and cash flow statement [F3]; the financing inference is drawn from the cash flow lines.
financial_health.claim: Cash uses are rising while operating cash flow is negative. Capital expenditure guidance for fiscal 2027 is $45.0 million to $50.0 million, versus $40.0 million to $45.0 million in the 10-K. The quarterly dividend is $0.13 per share, and dividends paid were (5,961) in the first quarter (table in thousands).
quotes: We currently expect to spend $45.0 million to $50.0 million on capital expenditures in fiscal 2027.

financial_health.basis: Stated in the MD&A of the 10-Q [P4] and 10-K [P3]; the finance lease term is from [P3].
financial_health.claim: Refinancing needs look distant on the evidence. The $175.0 million revolver matures on the earlier of October 3, 2029 or six months before the earliest maturity of any Permitted Notes, and $40.0 million was drawn at July 31, 2026. The material finance lease is payable in 240 monthly installments through fiscal 2039.
quotes: The Revolving Line matures on the earlier of October 3, 2029 or the date that is six months in advance of the earliest maturity of any Permitted Notes (as defined in the Second Amended and Restated Credit Agreement) under the Second Amended and Restated Credit Agreement.

financial_health.basis: Stated in the 8-K [P7]; funding and amounts are not visible.
financial_health.claim: The company completed the acquisition of Savage on October 21, 2026, after the latest balance sheet date. The visible text does not show how it was funded, so its effect on cash and debt is not measurable from this evidence.
quotes: On the Closing Date, the Company completed its acquisition of Savage pursuant to the Merger Agreement.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in the 10-Q MD&A (P4) and the 10-K MD&A (P3).
growth_thesis.claim: Handguns are the largest growth driver in the latest quarter: handgun sales rose $18.8 million, or 29.0%, in the three months ended July 31, 2026. For this to continue, consumer demand and sell-through at distributors and retailers must keep up with shipments.
quotes: Sales of our handguns increased $18.8 million, or 29.0%, over the comparable quarter last year

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in P4 and P3; the dependence on demand and mix is inferred from the share of new products.
growth_thesis.claim: Long guns rebounded in the latest quarter: sales rose $6.8 million, or 49.9%, after a 13.0% decline in fiscal 2026. For this to continue, the higher consumer demand and the mix shift to higher-priced models must persist.
quotes: Sales of our long guns increased $6.8 million, or 49.9%, over the comparable quarter last year

growth_thesis.basis: Shares and the plan are stated in P4, P3 and P1; the dependence on continued launches is inferred.
growth_thesis.claim: A steady flow of new products supports sales. New products were 35.3% of net sales in the latest quarter and 38.1% in fiscal 2026. For this to continue, the company must keep launching products that consumers accept.
quotes: Newly introduced products represented 35.3% of overall net sales for the three months ended July 31, 2026
We plan to continue to introduce new products in fiscal 2027.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in P4; the acceptance condition is inferred from the P2 risk factor.
growth_thesis.claim: Pricing is a contributing driver. A 2% to 3% price increase on select products took effect on January 1, 2026 and is cited as a reason for handgun sales growth. For this to continue, consumers must accept the higher prices without trading down.
quotes: a 2% to 3% price increase on select products that became effective on January 1, 2026

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in P4 and P6; the volume condition is inferred from the stated fixed-cost absorption benefit.
growth_thesis.claim: Gross margin expanded to 28.7% from 25.9%, but about 260 basis points came from a non-recurring $2.9 million tariff refund. Margin growth therefore depends on higher production volumes continuing to improve fixed-cost absorption, with labor cost and tariffs as offsets.
quotes: Excluding the impact of tariff refunds, gross margin for the three months ended July 31, 2026 was 26.1%.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in P4 and F2; the continuation condition is inferred.
growth_thesis.claim: Operating leverage turned operating income positive. Operating income rose $7.2 million, and operating expenses fell to 24.9% of sales from 29.4% because they grew 12.1% against sales growth of 32.3%. For this to continue, sales must keep outgrowing expense growth.
quotes: Operating income for the three months ended July 31, 2026 increased $7.2 million over the comparable quarter last year

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in the earnings release (P6) as management expectation; not a verified result.
growth_thesis.claim: Management guides to continued growth but at a slower pace than Q1: second-quarter sales roughly 10% above last year and fiscal 2027 revenue up approximately 5-7% over fiscal 2026, against 32.3% growth in Q1. This assumes a normal seasonal environment and strong product demand.
quotes: resulting in anticipated sales for the second quarter of roughly 10% above last year
For the full year, we continue to expect that our fiscal 2027 revenue will grow approximately 5-7% over fiscal 2026.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in P4; the dependence on sell-through is inferred from the 10-K inventory warning in P3.
growth_thesis.claim: The company is investing in capacity and building inventory ahead of expected demand. Q1 capital spending rose $7.6 million, mainly for machinery to expand capacity, and inventory rose $24.4 million. For this to pay off, the inventory must sell through as management expects.
quotes: largely for machinery and equipment to expand capacity and increase operational efficiency
We expect our inventory levels to build through the second quarter of fiscal 2027 and then decline during the remainder of the fiscal year.

growth_thesis.basis: The completion is stated in P7; its role as a growth driver is inferred, and the consideration terms were cut from the packet.
growth_thesis.claim: The Savage acquisition, completed October 21, 2026, is a potential additional growth source. The evidence does not show its size, price or earnings.
quotes: On the Closing Date, the Company completed its acquisition of Savage pursuant to the Merger Agreement.

material_events.basis: stated in the 8-K Items 1.01 and 2.01 text
material_events.claim: The company signed a merger agreement and completed its acquisition of Savage on the same day. Savage was merged into the company through a two-step merger, and the seller's designee was appointed to the board.
quotes: On the Closing Date, the Company completed its acquisition of Savage pursuant to the Merger Agreement.

material_events.basis: stated in the earnings release and the 10-Q MD&A
material_events.claim: In the first quarter of fiscal 2027, the company received tariff refunds that raised gross margin by about 260 basis points. It describes this as a non-recurring benefit.
quotes: These refunds favorably impacted gross margin by approximately 260 basis points and represented a non-recurring benefit.

risks.basis: Figures are stated in the 10-Q MD&A and statements. The link from inventory build to funding need is inferred from the cash flow statement and MD&A.
risks.claim: Q1 operating cash flow was negative at $8.8 million while inventory rose $24.4 million and revolver borrowings outstanding reached $40.0 million, against a $175.0 million line.
quotes: Inventory balances increased $24.4 million between April 30, 2026 and July 31, 2026 as a result of level loading of our manufacturing facilities to ensure our ability to satisfy anticipated future demand.

risks.basis: Stated in the 10-Q MD&A and the earnings release.
risks.claim: Q1 gross margin of 28.7% was lifted by about 260 basis points from non-recurring tariff refunds of $2.9 million. Excluding them, gross margin was 26.1%.
quotes: These refunds favorably impacted gross margin by approximately 260 basis points and represented a non-recurring benefit.

risks.basis: Guidance and the risk language are stated. That they imply deceleration is inferred by comparing the figures.
risks.claim: The sharp Q1 sales growth of 32.3% may not persist: company guidance points to slower growth (about 10% in Q2, 5-7% for the full year), and the 10-K says demand tends to soften after concerns subside.
quotes: These concerns often result in an increase in near-term consumer demand for our products and subsequent softening of demand when these concerns subside.

risks.basis: Stated in the 10-K risk factors and MD&A.
risks.claim: Tariff exposure remains uncertain: higher tariffs cost about 100 basis points of gross margin in fiscal 2026, and the amount and timing of further IEEPA refunds are unresolved.
quotes: In February 2026, the U.S. Supreme Court issued a ruling limiting the authority of the United States to impose tariffs under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act, creating uncertainty regarding tariffs previously assessed under that statute.

risks.basis: The closing and board appointment are stated. The risk mechanisms are inferred and no deal terms are visible.
risks.claim: The completed acquisition of Savage adds integration and financing-structure risk that the available text does not quantify.
quotes: On the Closing Date, the Company completed its acquisition of Savage pursuant to the Merger Agreement.

risks.basis: The risk is stated in the 10-K risk factors. Whether it is likely is not stated.
risks.claim: Tennessee relocation incentives carry a repayment risk if spending, headcount and wage commitments are not met.
quotes: If we fail to meet the performance requirements of the award, we may be required to repay all or a portion of the award amount.

unresolved_questions.basis: Inferred: the deal terms sit in omitted text; the item states only that the closing occurred.
unresolved_questions.claim: What did the Savage acquisition cost, how was it paid for, and what does Savage add to sales, margins and leverage? The retained text does not give the Merger Consideration or Savage's financials.
quotes: On the Closing Date, the Company completed its acquisition of Savage pursuant to the Merger Agreement.

unresolved_questions.basis: Stated in P4 and P6; the future refund path is inferred from the P2 risk language.
unresolved_questions.claim: How much of the 28.7% first-quarter gross margin will recur? It included $2.9 million of non-recurring tariff refunds, and the ex-refund margin was 26.1%. Whether further refunds will come is uncertain.
quotes: Excluding the impact of tariff refunds, gross margin for the three months ended July 31, 2026 was 26.1%.

unresolved_questions.basis: Stated in P4 for the inventory plan; the link to borrowings is inferred from F3.
unresolved_questions.claim: Will the inventory build turn into sales and cash, and will revolver borrowings come back down? Inventory rose $24.4 million in the quarter, borrowings outstanding reached $40.0 million, and free cash flow was negative.
quotes: We expect our inventory levels to build through the second quarter of fiscal 2027 and then decline during the remainder of the fiscal year.

unresolved_questions.basis: Stated: both ranges appear in the items; the cause of the change is not stated.
unresolved_questions.claim: Why did fiscal 2027 capital expenditure guidance rise from the 10-K range to the 10-Q range, and does the Savage deal change it again?
quotes: We currently expect to spend $45.0 million to $50.0 million on capital expenditures in fiscal 2027.

unresolved_questions.basis: Inferred from the dates of P6 and P7; the guidance figures are stated in P6.
unresolved_questions.claim: Does the full-year revenue growth outlook of 5-7% cover Savage? The first quarter grew 32.3%, so the outlook implies much slower growth ahead. Management said the guidance was made before the October 21 deal closing, and the sustainability of demand is unsettled.
quotes: For the full year, we continue to expect that our fiscal 2027 revenue will grow approximately 5-7% over fiscal 2026.

unresolved_questions.basis: Inferred from the Item 3.02 heading in the P7 title; terms are in omitted text.
unresolved_questions.claim: How many shares, if any, were issued to the Seller, and what are the Investor Rights Agreement terms? The 8-K heading lists Item 3.02 and a Seller-designated director was appointed, but share issuance amounts are not visible.
quotes: The information set forth in Item 1.01 of this Current Report on Form 8-K regarding the Seller’s right to designate a director under the Investor Rights Agreement is incorporated by reference into this Item 5.02.

unresolved_questions.basis: Stated for the expiry date; the renewal status is not in any item.
unresolved_questions.claim: Will the buyback authorization be renewed? The 2025 authorization ran only through September 21, 2026, and no shares were repurchased under it in the evidence period.
quotes: On September 15, 2025, our Board of Directors authorized the repurchase of up to $50.0 million of our common stock, subject to certain conditions, in the open market or in privately negotiated transactions from September 21, 2025 through September 21, 2026, or the 2025 Authorization.

unresolved_questions.basis: Stated in P2 and P4 for the existence of the suits and higher legal costs; the amounts are not given.
unresolved_questions.claim: How large is the legal exposure behind higher G&A? General and administrative costs rose partly on higher legal costs, and the company is a defendant in a state "firearm industry responsibility" action and a privacy class action.
quotes: These statutes are being actively enforced, and we are a defendant in one such action.

unresolved_questions.basis: Stated risk in P2; progress against the requirements is not stated.
unresolved_questions.claim: Will the company meet the Tennessee incentive performance requirements at the January 1, 2027, 2028 and 2029 compliance dates, or must it repay any of the award? The award amount is not stated in the retained text.
quotes: If we fail to meet the performance requirements of the award, we may be required to repay all or a portion of the award amount.

P6.s23.text: Deana McPherson, Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer, commented, "We continue to expect a normal seasonal environment and strong demand for our products, resulting in anticipated sales for the second quarter of roughly 10% above last year.

P6.s24.text: For the full year, we continue to expect that our fiscal 2027 revenue will grow approximately 5-7% over fiscal 2026.

unknowns: The Savage acquisition closed on October 21, 2026, after the September 3 guidance. The evidence gives no revenue, margin or financing figures for Savage, so its effect on fiscal 2027 revenue and margins is not known.
It is not stated whether management has updated the 5-7% full-year revenue guidance since the acquisition.
The first-quarter margin includes a non-recurring $2.9 million tariff refund, and the first quarter is seasonally weak. The evidence does not give the full-year margin path.
Further tariff refunds, and their timing and size, are not known.

verdict_reason: expected return -35.1 points a year against the required return over 3 years
